title: Hacker Runs Hermes AI Agent Unattended for Post-Exploitation at Thai Finance Ministry

reading.body:
An autonomous AI agent called Hermes was deployed unattended to conduct post-exploitation activities against Thailand's Ministry of Finance. The system was used to enumerate the network, access data storage infrastructure, and target email and administrative systems after initial compromise. This represents a failure in detection and response, where an AI agent operated within a compromised network environment without human oversight or intervention.

The attack combined the AI agent with custom malware and exploited known vulnerabilities in widely used software. The operator maintained encrypted command channels and staged materials on external servers, indicating this was a deliberate, sustained campaign rather than an opportunistic breach. Detecting this would have required network monitoring to identify the AI agent's reconnaissance activity, anomalous data access patterns, and unauthorized attempts to exploit known software flaws.

It is not established whether the Ministry's own security systems failed to alert defenders in real time, or whether alerts were generated but not acted upon. The attribution to Chinese-linked operations is based on infrastructure associations and language references in attack materials, not on confirmed identity of the attackers.

summary:
# Summary

Thailand's Ministry of Finance fell victim to a cyberattack involving an autonomous AI agent named Hermes and a custom implant called Hades. Between July 9 and 13, 2026, researchers discovered three exposed directories on a Hong Kong server containing 585 files and 470 megabytes of attack materials, including exploit code, stolen credentials, and webshells. The operator deployed Hermes in unattended mode to enumerate the ministry's network, access Hadoop infrastructure, and target mail systems and administrative panels. The attack also leveraged multiple known vulnerabilities including flaws in sudo, polkit, and IIS WebDAV services.

The investigation revealed a sophisticated operation with detailed knowledge of the ministry's internal systems and network topology. The Hades implant, built in multiple Windows and Linux versions, communicated with command servers in Hong Kong and Malaysia using encrypted channels. Evidence suggests the attackers gained access to session cookies, deployed webshells, and compromised various internal services. Thailand's national security authorities were notified on July 15, 2026. The infrastructure involved was previously associated with other Chinese-linked cyber operations, and the presence of Chinese language references in the attack materials provided additional attribution clues.
